findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: entity_state, changes_since, coverage, search · Private data: entity_state, changes_since, timeline, coverage, search, trends, entity_diff, models, fetch · Public sink: timeline.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: entity_state, changes_since, coverage, search · Private data: entity_state, changes_since, timeline, coverage, search, trends, entity_diff, models, fetch · Public sink: timeline

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "entity_state" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
